scope: 12 purposively selected complete cases from the existing 30-short study; research, not performance ranking or render qualification

cases.title: Claude Can Now Plan Your Whole Day by Location
cases.lesson: A location-aware day planner should reason about specific stops, distances, routes and ordering instead of offering an unconnected list; the visual presentation should make those relationships inspectable.
cases.opening: The spoken novelty is Claude gaining location awareness through MapQuest MCP. Familiar logos identify the combination, then route alternatives provide a visible preview of its promise. It is a capability reveal, not a separate contrarian title card.
cases.story_arc: Name the integration → preview route output → unpack nearby/distance/time/traffic with matching capability visuals → establish one-day New York scenario → display a cumulative prompt → reject random recommendations → illustrate places, routes, ordering and a five-minute trip → show destination experience → broaden to other agents → offer access and keyword CTA.
cases.payoff: The viewer sees how spatial relationships can make a day plan useful and sees the shape of relevant inputs/results. A single continuous executed New York itinerary is not demonstrated: city/rendition changes and generic stop lists leave that proof unclosed.
cases.selection_reason: A complete example of the same split host supporting many distinct informational jobs, a justified 4.5-second input hold, UI-detail enlargement, destination B-roll, and a digit-plus-unit incentive. It also exposes the risk of visually plausible but task-inconsistent map assets.
cases.review_limits: Viewed all 5 chronological 0.5-second context pages (90 samples including final frame) plus 90 framing samples on 10 extra strips. Original machine-caption grouping supplies spoken ideas; no audio audition or phonetic verification. Caption final word overruns video; source was not padded or retimed. Strip timestamps are ffmpeg eight-fps resampling estimates, not source-frame measurements. Continuous motion, exact typography, easing, generation provenance and product claims are not independently verified. Catalog source inspection supports possible mechanisms only; no rendered match or ready replica is claimed.

cases.title: I Gave an AI Engineer Access to My Whole Business
cases.lesson: Persistent business context plus a concrete request can produce a relevant deliverable; a strong edit connects the source information, constraints and visible result, then explains the resulting workflow benefit.
cases.opening: The hook names a high-stakes existing object—one repository for the creator’s business—and asks what happens when Devin gets access. A red arrow/repository view and working-person cut make the object and owner concrete before the agent is named.
cases.story_arc: Establish business repo → name agent and environment → montage claimed indexing/wiki artifacts → reset to one concrete waitlist request → show program and brand sources → show matching page → spotlight result → introduce Slack participation and conceptual parallelism → return to repository as the reason repeated explanation is avoided → preview setup resource.
cases.payoff: The concrete waitlist page visibly answers the request and reflects the supplied branding. Several intervening images illustrate categories rather than proving the exact claims: planner for browser, code diff for wiki, generic graph/document for repo knowledge, and a website form for pull request.
cases.selection_reason: A complete task-to-result story with real constraint artifacts, reusable split layout, two distinct attention spotlights, an opening-object callback and tangible CTA preview. Its mismatched filler images and decorative parallel-worker close view show what a directing library should flag rather than imitate.
cases.review_limits: Viewed all 4 chronological 0.5-second context pages (70 samples including final frame) plus 69 framing samples on 8 extra strips. Original machine-caption grouping supplies spoken ideas; no audio audition or phonetic verification. Caption final word overruns video; source was not padded or retimed. Strip timestamps are ffmpeg eight-fps resampling estimates, not source-frame measurements. Continuous motion, exact typography, easing, generation provenance and product claims are not independently verified. Catalog source inspection supports possible mechanisms only; no rendered match or ready replica is claimed.

cases.title: This AI Cloned Me in 15 Seconds
cases.lesson: A short identity source can be reused as concrete output variations: preserve the same person while changing outfit or setting, compare variants for reuse, and show the specific constraint solved by studio-looking content while away.
cases.opening: The spoken hook claims this AI cloned the creator in fifteen seconds. A face mesh, scan line and obscured logo turn the claim into an identity-capture puzzle; the later HeyGen reveal names the mechanism. The scan is a visual metaphor and the actual input/output comparison must carry the demonstration.
cases.story_arc: Identity hook/metaphorical scan → explanatory narrator → actual short source excerpt → name tool → compare narrator with claimed twin → isolate outfit then background changes → show new speaking output and avoided camera step → explain successful-content variations → show three versions → explain travel constraint with two-setting comparison → give output face space for fidelity claim → broaden to two different creator examples → brand/keyword CTA.
cases.payoff: Viewers can see the same-person continuity across different clothing/settings and understand why reuse or away-from-studio production is useful. Actual generation time, source lineage, voice fidelity, hook-test outcomes and realism are not independently verified by this sampled visual study.
cases.selection_reason: The strongest identity/state-continuity example in this assignment: a nearly four-second simultaneous comparison, widening wardrobe/background reveals, three output bands, a travel-versus-studio contrast, literal avoided-camera B-roll and a held close face for detail evaluation.
cases.review_limits: Viewed all 4 chronological 0.5-second context pages (77 samples including final frame) plus 90 framing samples on 10 extra strips. Original machine-caption grouping supplies spoken ideas; no audio audition or phonetic verification. Caption final word overruns video; source was not padded or retimed. Strip timestamps are ffmpeg eight-fps resampling estimates, not source-frame measurements. Continuous motion, exact typography, easing, generation provenance and product claims are not independently verified. Catalog source inspection supports possible mechanisms only; no rendered match or ready replica is claimed. One additional original-resolution opening frame at approximately 0.1 seconds was inspected to distinguish the face mesh, pixelated logo and arrow.

cases.title: Practice Any Hard Conversation Before It Matters
cases.lesson: Skill acquisition needs rehearsal of the actual conversation, not only consuming information about it. The visual argument transfers boxing practice to an upcoming sales call.
cases.opening: A presenter challenge rejects watching boxing videos and immediately entering the ring. Gym and ring images make the familiar skill gap concrete before it is applied to work.
cases.story_arc: Boxing analogy → passive workplace training → knowledge/performance distinction → roleplay product → scheduled sales call → human/avatar rehearsal → claimed feedback and repeat attempt → broader uses → watch-versus-practise callback → comment CTA.
cases.payoff: The comparison delivers a clear reason to rehearse and a recognisable practice interface. It does not demonstrate responsive pushback, personalised correction or measured improvement; the analytics insert is engagement data.
cases.selection_reason: Shows a complete analogy-to-scenario structure, repeated presenter returns, paired human/interface splits, one precise calendar spotlight, an accumulating scope graphic and a closing visual callback. It also shows where plausible imagery fails to prove the exact words.
cases.review_limits: Complete chronological 2 fps contextual sheets were visually inspected, with narrow calendar and presenter strips sampled every sixth decoded source frame and a full-resolution analytics frame. The strip manifests record source frame indices and PTS from the native scan. No audio audition in this expansion; spoken ideas are paraphrases from timed caption sidecars checked against visible context. Boundaries are approximate editorial partitions, generally within 0.5-second contextual spacing; exact-index strips refine only inspected intervals. Exact easing and word lock are not claimed. The automatic transcript extends past the 43.933333-second visual rendition, so coverage ends at the observed media duration. These are source observations and planning guidance, not a rendered replica or qualified template.

cases.title: Never Miss a Customer Call Again (AI Receptionist)
cases.lesson: Repeated customer questions and unanswered calls consume attention; the useful product story should show a relevant inquiry becoming an answer, booking or handoff, then explain the human benefit.
cases.opening: An unanswered-call scenario is paired with a negative colour cue, then a competitor consequence. This gives the viewer a recognisable business cost before the personal event example.
cases.story_arc: Missed call → competitor risk → personal virtual event → underestimated question volume → impatient customers → receptionist introduction → question/answer and channel examples → booking/FAQ/routing claims → busy-team fallback → language claim → worried-versus-focused owner contrast → branded trial CTA.
cases.payoff: The short makes the workload and desired benefit concrete and shows several recognisable interface examples. It does not prove the numerical booking count, automatic answering, multilingual fluency or customer outcomes; some example screens do not match the current spoken claim.
cases.selection_reason: A dense full-length mix of human problem scenes, split product orientation, progressive question cards, one local avatar selection, a targeted call-control pointer, numeric emphasis, short demonstrations and a human outcome contrast. It distinguishes new pictures from actual action/result evidence.
cases.review_limits: All six chronological 2 fps context pages were inspected, plus avatar-selection and call-focus strips sampled every sixth decoded source frame and a full-resolution messaging frame. The strip manifests preserve frame indices and PTS from the native scan. Audio was not auditioned in this expansion. Spoken ideas come from timed caption sidecars checked against visible context; their timestamps contain anomalies and extend past the 55.933333-second visual rendition. Beat boundaries are approximate editorial partitions, not verified source edit points; exact-index strips refine only inspected intervals. No easing, response authenticity or unseen click result is claimed. These are source observations and proposed planning decisions, not a rendered replica or qualified template.

cases.title: I Build Features Just By Talking to My Code
cases.lesson: A process short can make an abstract interaction understandable by showing the trigger, the complete input, questions, approval and visible output. The input needs a sustained read window, and every later result must belong to that same input.
cases.opening: The surprising spoken premise is talking to code. A /voice title and headphones on a product mascot cue listening, then a Space keycap identifies the trigger before the input window appears.
cases.story_arc: Voice premise → spacebar action → long prompt accumulation → plan/activity montage → questions → research phase → approval condition and human approval illustration → model identity → build/test montage → website tour → completion cue → teammate metaphor → product CTA.
cases.payoff: The short makes voice-to-request and the intended process stages recognisable. It does not close the opening dashboard request with a matching dashboard result: the shown output is a Mars registration website. Approval order, actual clarifying-question direction and successful verification are also not demonstrated cleanly.
cases.selection_reason: Provides the strongest contrast to a two-second editing metronome: one input scene holds for more than six seconds after its brief entrance. It also distinguishes a whole-window enlargement, small keycap emphasis, accumulating questions, native UI scrolling and completion overlays from separate layout changes.
cases.review_limits: All four complete chronological 2 fps context pages were inspected, plus three narrow 10 fps strips regenerated from explicit decoded source frame indices and a full-resolution output frame. No audio audition in this expansion. Spoken ideas are paraphrases of timed caption sidecars checked against the visible sequence. Beat boundaries remain approximate editorial partitions, generally within 0.5-second contextual spacing; exact frame-index strip labels support only the inspected intervals. No easing or word-perfect synchronisation is claimed. Machine captions extend beyond the visual duration; coverage ends at 30.1 seconds. These are source observations and proposed planning decisions, not a rendered replica or qualified template.

cases.title: Give ChatGPT and Claude the Same Memory
cases.lesson: A remembered object can be asked for in another model; the edit teaches this through a same-object input/response test, then a shared-memory model.
cases.opening: Presenter promises cross-model memory; a typed app name and terminal-stack Memory graphic quickly label the endpoints and concept.
cases.story_arc: Promise → repeated-context inconvenience → create/connect/remember → ask the same object in ChatGPT → returned guideline card → shared-center explanation → control assurances and testimony → link CTA.
cases.payoff: The returned asset card pays off the same-object question. Encryption and model-specific access are asserted but not demonstrated; late coding/shopping footage does not close that gap.
cases.selection_reason: Shows a useful input→same-object→returned-artifact chain, a real whole-diagram enlargement and hold, and the difference between concrete demonstration and generic technical B-roll.
cases.review_limits: All four chronological 0.5s sheets (76 sampled frames) were visually opened, plus six 6fps strips. This is full-duration sampled coverage, not every source frame reviewed. Video is 1080x1920/60fps; no audio audition. Spoken ideas use machine VTT alignment and visible captions; tail overrun is excluded from exact timing claims. Motion observations do not establish easing. Product/security assertions and catalog replica readiness are not verified.

cases.title: Huge ChatGPT Update You Need to See!
cases.lesson: The reference distinguishes question answering, developer work and longer project execution, then illustrates a morning chief-of-staff use case with multiple inputs and priority categories.
cases.opening: Typed ChatGPT name over presenter → chat screen with red X → OpenAI identity → presentation being edited. The sequence makes a category-change claim and quickly supplies an artifact example.
cases.story_arc: Category reversal → three app roles → connected apps and device access → chief-of-staff topology → scheduled input review → asserted morning plan and priority categories → manual/automated contrast → additional execution examples → download CTA.
cases.payoff: Several visible work artifacts support the broad execution category. The chief-of-staff example stops at status and abstract priority labels; its actual morning plan is not revealed. Shopping, product analytics and generic desk footage sometimes lose the specific spoken example.
cases.selection_reason: Provides a long fast sequence with role comparisons, source-input cards, real branch/output/return topology, same-scene annotation and a meaningful several-second explanatory hold. It also exposes where activity substitutes for proof.
cases.review_limits: All six chronological 0.5s context sheets were opened through the final frame, plus four selected 6fps strips. Full-duration sampled visual coverage, not every-frame review or audio listening. Machine transcript supplies approximate speech alignment. Claims about OpenAI features, availability and counts are recorded as reference claims and not independently verified. Still strips support observed change but not exact easing. Catalog sources supply partial mechanisms, not ready replicas.

cases.title: OpenArt Director: The New Way to Make AI Videos
cases.lesson: The proposed workflow directs a project through text, story and character objects rather than stopping at one clip; project timeline context is the clearest evidence of the multi-shot unit.
cases.opening: Output beauty, street and action shots above the presenter build appeal, then OpenArt identity and a directing metaphor lead to the Vibe Directing name.
cases.story_arc: Output appeal → category name → one-clip/whole-sequence comparison → prompt/story/character/pacing surfaces → coherent action sequence and lifestyle continuity examples → multi-clip editor preview → interpretation and creator relevance → product/link CTA.
cases.payoff: The source makes the project-level idea concrete with planning objects and a timeline around related shots. It does not show a complete requested revision propagating, verify one-run/five-minute generation, or prove stable voices. Character/style examples are suggestive visual evidence with provenance limits.
cases.selection_reason: Separates generated-footage movement from editorial zoom; includes a horizontal character-reference pan, sequence continuity through retained subjects, and the difference between output spectacle and a visible project container.
cases.review_limits: All four chronological 0.5s sheets (65 samples including final frame) were opened, plus five selected 6fps seek-based strips. This is complete-duration sampled visual coverage, not every-source-frame review. No audio listening; speech meaning comes from timed machine captions and visible captions. Strip timestamps are approximate requested/fps-filter times, not measured source-frame PTS or exact cut boundaries. Footage provenance, voice consistency, generation duration and easing are unverified; VTT tail overrun is excluded from playable timing claims. Final delivery QA inspected native-PTS character-sheet captures and corrected an earlier face-zoom interpretation to a stable-scale lateral pan.

cases.title: ClickUp Brain2: The AI That Replaces All Your Software
cases.lesson: A workspace assistant is presented through familiar work artifacts, concrete input/output examples and a contextual task, with a replacement claim framing the pitch.
cases.opening: A ClickUp identity graphic becomes a crossed-out grid of other apps above the presenter. The visible contradiction supplies a reason to investigate the replacement claim. It is a promotional claim, not proven by the opening itself.
cases.story_arc: Promise fewer tools → establish personal use → illustrate replacement → introduce AI capabilities → show generated work and an expanded deck → develop a context-aware lunch request into a response → close with a promotional offer.
cases.payoff: The source shows several useful interfaces and artifacts, including a visible request-to-response chain. Most broad replacement and autonomous-work claims remain illustrative; the investor prompt and following deck are different examples.
cases.selection_reason: Adds a long produced Short with many changes of information inside retained layouts, an extended prompt build, a real preview enlargement, and a multi-part contextual result. It is useful for deciding when a screenshot, diagram, presenter or full UI deserves the frame.
cases.review_limits: Complete chronological 0.5-second source-frame sheets and machine-timed transcript inspected; listed native strips refine selected motions. No audio audition or uninterrupted realtime playback. Image-to-words reasoning is editorial interpretation, not known creator intent or retention evidence. Interval boundaries are approximate unless a native frame is cited.

cases.title: Businesses only care about 3 things: Money, Time, Focus  #artificialintelligence
cases.lesson: A buyer evaluates the destination and business outcome; the technology is the means of getting there.
cases.opening: The presenter names three business priorities, promising a simpler way to sell AI work. This is a spoken opening carried by a face; the early money badge is partly clipped and is not a strong standalone visual hook.
cases.story_arc: State buyer priorities → demonstrate destination versus interchangeable vehicles → return to interpret the analogy → reject the technical feature pitch → visualize leads without ads → restate the outcome rule.
cases.payoff: The taxi analogy earns the outcome-over-tool lesson. The bot and envelopes illustrate a proposed service; they do not establish qualified leads or customer results.
cases.selection_reason: Adds a coherent multi-picture analogy, a negative example, and an evolving system scene. It also shows why long presenter holds can coexist with fast visual runs. N30 reuses the outreach scene, so it is not counted as independent evidence here.
cases.review_limits: Complete chronological 0.5-second source-frame sheets and machine-timed transcript inspected; listed native strips refine selected motions. No audio audition or uninterrupted realtime playback. Image-to-words reasoning is editorial interpretation, not known creator intent or retention evidence. Interval boundaries are approximate unless a native frame is cited.

cases.title: Price your AI agents so it is a no-brainer for the client  #artificialintelligence
cases.lesson: Diagnose a measurable business problem, calculate outcome value, then price the solution in relation to that value.
cases.opening: The opening immediately begins a worked pricing example. A presenter and developing arithmetic establish a useful calculation, rather than an unrelated title card.
cases.story_arc: Diagnose lost time → show automation and annual value → compare the price with that value → use a contractor analogy to contrast tools with outcomes → show a promised gain and shorter time → return to a practical discovery-call behavior.
cases.payoff: The visual argument connects value to price and gives example diagnostic questions. The side calculation and ending are cropped; transfer the method with all operands and units legible and a complete closing thought.
cases.selection_reason: Adds cumulative calculation, simultaneous value/price comparison, a multi-object negative example, a number animation, a shortening duration bar and a simulated dialogue. These supply mechanisms beyond product screenshots.
cases.review_limits: Complete chronological 0.5-second source-frame sheets and machine-timed transcript inspected; listed native strips refine selected motions. No audio audition or uninterrupted realtime playback. Image-to-words reasoning is editorial interpretation, not known creator intent or retention evidence. Interval boundaries are approximate unless a native frame is cited.
